title: Guided alignment
ended: Guide ended. You can start it again at any time: Turntable check → Guided first alignment.
welcome_text: This station has no measured turntable yet. Would you like to align your turntable for the first time? The guide takes you through it step by step:
welcome_pending: The measurement of “{name}” is not finished yet. Would you like to go on where you stopped?
outline_record: Choose your test record, or describe it.
outline_profile: Enter the turntable: cartridge, recording device, tracking force.
outline_measure: Measure: the noise of the chain, then the sides of the test record.
outline_verdict: The verdict: ready to measure records, or what to adjust first, with a guide for each point.
welcome_time: It takes about 20–30 minutes. You can stop at any time and go on later.
record_title: Which test record do you have?
record_text: vinyl-check finds the bands of a test record by their signal, so their order and the announcements do not matter. With the AAPT 1 every finding has been checked on real recordings; with the others, bands of the known kinds are recognised, but not yet checked on a recording of that record.
other_text: Not in the list? Enter its key data: name, speed, sides, and which kinds of bands the sleeve lists.
none_title: I don't have a test record
none_text: What a test record is for, which one to get, and how to start without one.
custom_text: Tick the kinds of bands the sleeve lists. vinyl-check recognises a band by its signal, so order and announcements do not matter, but the band must match the description.
custom_name_placeholder: e.g. the test LP from the shelf
custom_hint: To be accepted as the reference of a turntable, the record needs at least the 1 kHz reference tone on both channels.
custom_saved_no_reference: Saved. Without a 1 kHz reference tone, vinyl-check can measure parts of the set-up but cannot accept the turntable with this record.
none_why: A test record carries exactly defined tones: a reference level, one channel at a time, a speed tone, a rising level for anti-skating. From what comes back, vinyl-check sees how the turntable is set up, instead of guessing from music.
none_recommend: vinyl-check was built and checked with {name} by Analogue Productions: with it, every finding of the station is available.
none_others: The other records in the list work in part. Older or very cheap test records often lack the bands vinyl-check needs: a 1 kHz tone on one channel only, 3150 Hz, a rising level ramp.
none_without: You can still check records: vinyl-check then uses standard values (reference −20 dBFS, nominal speed). Set up the turntable by the maker's figures, measure the noise of the chain once with Calibration (stylus up), and check the level on a loud record. Come back to the guided alignment when you have a test record.
basics_title: Before you measure: the basic set-up
basics_text: The measurement shows how well the turntable is set up and works best when the basics are right. Open the guide for each step you have not done yet.
verdict_ready_text: Every figure that matters for measuring records is within its target. Accept the result: from then on vinyl-check evaluates every recording with this turntable using these values.
verdict_ready_notes_text: Nothing stands in the way of measuring records. A few figures could be better, each with a guide below. Adjust them now or later, then record the affected side again.
verdict_adjust_text: Some figures are out of range and would distort what vinyl-check measures on records. Each has a guide below; after adjusting, record the affected side again. You can also accept anyway and adjust later.
verdict_remeasure_text: Bands that matter for measuring records were not recognised (see Not found), so the turntable cannot be judged on them yet. Record that side again; you can also accept anyway.
verdict_incomplete_text: The result cannot be accepted yet.
incomplete_calibration: The noise of the chain has not been measured (step Calibrate chain).
incomplete_reference: The 1 kHz reference tone was not found. Record the side with the reference tone again, and check the level if it is very quiet or clipped.
incomplete_record_reference: This test record has no 1 kHz tone on both channels at a reference level. The findings help with adjusting; to accept the turntable, measure with a test record that has one.
list_notes_hint: These depend mostly on the phono stage, the cartridge or the room, and do not change what the record check counts.
missing_hint: The test record has these bands, but they were not recognised. Record the side again: a band is missed when the stylus was lowered late or the recording stopped early.
list_not_covered: Not measured with this test record
not_covered_hint: Your test record has no bands for these settings. Set them by the maker's figures:
accept_anyway_confirm: Some figures are still out of range. Accept the result anyway? You can measure again at any time (Measure again).
done_ready_text: Every figure that matters for measuring records is within its target.
done_ready_notes_text: Good enough to measure records. A few figures could be better, each with a guide below; after adjusting, choose Measure again.
done_adjust_text: Some figures are out of range and distort what vinyl-check measures on records. Each has a guide below; after adjusting, choose Measure again.
done_remeasure_text: Bands that matter for measuring records were not recognised when the turntable was measured (see Not found). Choose Choose Measure again to measure them.
done_incomplete_text: The reference of this turntable is incomplete.
missing_hint_done: The test record has these bands, but they were not recognised in the accepted run. Choose Measure again to measure them.
finish_title: Done: you can measure records now
finish_text: “{name}” is measured. Every recording with this turntable now uses its reference level, speed, chain noise and click floor.
finish_text_open: The turntable is accepted, but some points are still open. Records can be measured; the open points and their guides stay on the turntable's page. Afterwards, choose Measure again.
finish_next: Next: put on a record, choose it under Record check and record a whole side.
